items.title: Lionel Reason Interview, 1981-05-26
items.q: His name was Aban. Your school and the quality of your teaching.

ctx.x: I met you there. We were in music school together. Yeah.

And, um, I was interested in going there because I wanted to take up, um, a, a stuffy stuff They haven't had another lesson since then and they raised their own family and just from what I taught them they became a professional musician. So I see them now, they wanted to call me, they didn't know whether they should call me Mr. Reason. I see that, so one boy by the name of Joe Dutry said, I tell you we're going to call him Pops. And I started those boys off and one of the boys, the little white boy, the young…

at LSU and he made first chair. And he told me that the instructor didn't believe he took music lessons in Liberia. So his daddy said I told him it wasn't New Iberia, it was the man who was teaching it. His name was Aban. Your school and the quality of your teaching. Yeah. And the home, I rented a six room house on Madison Slew. And the man who owned the house sold the house without telling me he was going to sell it. And so I moved to a small single house and I stopped teaching. And I just kept a few students.…
